Code Defect: When adding `<script>` or `<link>` tags that load resources from an external CDN (e.g., in `src/docs/index.html`), always include a Subresource Integrity (SRI) `integrity` attribute with the cryptographic hash of the resource, plus a matching `crossorigin` attribute. Loading CDN assets without an integrity check exposes users to supply-chain attacks.

In async rendering loops in diagram-dispatching code (e.g., `mermaid.ts`), do not use `Promise.all` for parallel `render` calls. Diagram database modules (e.g., `flowDb.js`) rely on module-level mutable state, so concurrent renders corrupt each other's output. Sequential `await` is required. This is a known architectural limitation tracked in issue #3577.

When documentation code examples reference mermaid via CDN, always include an explicit version pin. In source files under `packages/mermaid/src/docs/` processed by the `docs.mts` build transform, use the `<MERMAID_VERSION>` placeholder. In files served directly (e.g., standalone HTML in `vdocs/`), hardcode the current major version (e.g., `@9`). Unversioned CDN URLs break archived docs when a new major version is released.

When adding or reviewing code examples in documentation that reference mermaid module file paths, verify filenames are correctly spelled — e.g., the ESM build artifact is `mermaid.esm.mjs`, not `mermaid.ems.mjs`.

When modifying header-generation logic in `packages/mermaid/src/docs.mts`, verify that the relative path in the autogenerated 'DO NOT EDIT' source-file link is derived from the *output* file's directory depth under `docs/`, not from the source file path. Spot-check generated headers for at least one top-level file and one subdirectory file.

Pre-release version identifiers in semver strings must include a dot before the numeric component (e.g., `9.2.1-rc.1`, not `9.2.1-rc1`). Without the dot, identifiers are compared lexicographically, causing `rc10 < rc9`. Verify this format whenever `package.json` version fields are modified.

When refactoring a callback from a function parameter into an optional interface property, verify that at least one concrete implementation actually sets that property before adding a conditional guard in the calling code. If no implementation sets it, remove the branch rather than leaving dead code.

When adding or modifying entries in the redirect map (`packages/mermaid/src/docs/.vitepress/theme/redirect.ts`), verify that every non-empty target path resolves to an actual, content-bearing documentation page; spot-check target URLs in the running dev server before merging.

Use `window.location.replace()` instead of assigning to `window.location.href` when performing client-side redirects, so the source URL is not pushed onto the browser history stack and users can navigate back without being caught in a redirect loop.
Maintainability and Readability: When destructuring but discarding one of the destructured variables (e.g., using `Object.entries` when only the value is needed), prefer an alternative that avoids unused variables (e.g., `Object.values`) to prevent `no-unused-vars` lint warnings.

When adding ESLint `overrides` in `.eslintrc.json` to suppress rules for test/spec files (e.g., `*.spec.{ts,js}`, `cypress/**`, `docs/**` globs), prefer setting rules to `"warn"` rather than `"off"` so newly introduced violations still appear in PR diffs; only use `"off"` when accumulated warning count is large enough to obscure real errors.

CI status badges in README files (`README.md`, `README.zh-CN.md`, `docs/README.md`, and other variants) must link to the currently active CI system (GitHub Actions). When updating any one README, check that all sibling README variants receive the same badge update.

Variables in `packages/mermaid/src/docs.mts` that hold a specific semver component must be named to reflect which component they contain (e.g., `MERMAID_MAJOR_VERSION` for just the major version, not a generic `mermaidVersion`).

When deprecating or removing public-facing config options, API methods, or package exports, document the change in the CHANGELOG or release notes — not only via in-code deprecation warnings — so existing consumers have clear migration guidance.

When a feature, config key, or code path is removed or replaced, audit all related JSDoc blocks and inline comments and remove or update any references to the old feature; stale documentation misleads future contributors.

When adding routing or navigation behavior inside the VitePress theme's `enhanceApp` hook (`packages/mermaid/src/docs/.vitepress/theme/index.ts`), prefer using VitePress's official router API (e.g., the `router` object from the `ctx` argument) over directly patching router lifecycle callbacks.
Performance Issue: When reviewing changes to build entry points in `.esbuild/util.cjs` (or any esbuild build configuration), verify that each new entry point is intentional and explicitly justified: each additional entry point produces a full separate bundle in `dist/`, potentially adding tens of megabytes to the output.
Code Style: Proofread prose in JSDoc comments and documentation for grammar errors, including wrong word choices (e.g., 'In one is provided' → 'If one is provided') and subject-verb agreement (e.g., 'This prevent' → 'This prevents').
In GitHub Actions workflow YAML files, when a step needs to execute from a specific directory, use the `working-directory` step attribute rather than embedding a `cd` command inside the `run:` block.
